newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: INTERVIEW-Noble commodity group to grow 25 pct '97.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Noble commodity group to grow 25 pct '97.

text.p: Asian commodity company Noble Group Ltd is set for strong growth over the next few years as it expands the range and volume of the raw materials it distributes, company executives and analysts said on Thursday.

Announcing the terms of its Singapore initial public share offer (IPO), chairman Richard Elman said Noble planned to diversify into new areas and strengthen its already dominant position in the Chinese market.

"The growth will come from all the diverse commodity divisions: from iron ore transportation, steel intermediate and finished products, alumina, fertilisers and coal and coke," Elman told Reuters in an interview.
Founded in 1986, Hong Kong-based Noble sources, transports, finances and delivers a range of commodities from primary producers to processors and end-users.
The company has grown rapidly over the past five years. Its net profit rose to US$19.8 million in 1995 from around $500,000 in 1991. Turnover in 1995 was $595.5 million.

Growth slowed in 1996 because of a slump in the value of many commodities and a fall in shipping rates. As a result, the company expected a net profit of $20.2 million for the year to December 31, 1996, the IPO prospectus said.

Elman declined to forecast Noble's profit growth but Richard Stokes, director of regional marine research at W.I. Carr, joint lead manager for the share issue, said he expected growth to pick up again strongly over the next two years.
"In 1997, we are going for 25 percent earnings growth to $25.2 million, and then in 1998 we are going for a further 22 percent earnings growth to $30.8 million," he told Reuters.
Elman said Noble's coal and coke division, which the company bought in December 1996 from Salomon Brothers, should experience strong growth as the market expands in China and across Asia.
He said Asian demand for coal was 136 million tonnes in 1996 and was expected to rise to 304 million tonnes by 2010.
"This clearly indicates the phenomenal growth prospects for our coal and coke division," he told a briefing on the IPO.
Other areas were also expanding fast.
He said Noble currently handles up to a quarter of China's 45 million tonnes of iron ore imports, 10 percent of its steel imports and 25-35 percent of its ferro-chrome exports.
Elman said the prospects for profit growth were excellent.
"Asia is the world's fastest growing commodity market," he said. "So long as Asia's infrastructure grows, demand for our services will as well."

Noble is offering 51.49 million shares at US$0.88 each in its Singapore share offer. Of this total, 10.30 million shares are offered to the public and 41.19 million for placement. All the placement shares have already been taken up.

The IPO is expected to raise net proceeds of $39.4 million, of which approximately $10 million will be used to expand the group's range of products and $10 million used to acquire vessels to expand the group's shipping business.
